question: Why do young women in cities struggle to find work?

brief.question: Why do young women in cities struggle to find work?
brief.answer: Young women in urban areas have very low labour market attachment: in 2025 only 23.2% of urban 15‑29‑year‑old women were in the labour force versus 60.9% of men, a gender gap of –37.7 points (narrowed slightly by 0.3 points since 2024). At the same time their unemployment is higher, with an urban female‑male gap of +7.1 percentage points (women 18.9% vs men 11.8%), which widened by 0.3 points since 2024. The largest gaps are seen in states such as Dadra & Nagar Haveli & Daman & Diu (LFPR gap –53.1 points) and Bihar (UR gap +27.1 points). These figures show that young urban women are far less likely to be participating in work and, when they do, face higher unemployment, indicating a struggle to find work.
